heading: Identification & "Consubstantiality"
role_in_volume: KEYSTONE — TRIPLE-PASS. The substantive opening of the Rhetoric: Burke redefines rhetoric's master term from 'persuasion' to 'identification', grounds identification in the substance-theoretic notion of 'consubstantiality' carried over from the Grammar, and shows identification operating through property, the 'autonomous' specialty, the rhetoric of self-address, and (reframing) primitive magic. THIS UNIT HOUSES the consubstantiation↔incorporation bridge — the motive-mechanism beneath Calleja's incorporation that the Grammar pipeline flagged as 'pending-future-rhetoric-of-motives-pipeline' (gm-pentad-operationalization-manual Section E).

phase2_pass_log.pass_2_complete: Identification redefinition fully operationalized (A-identified-with-B via shared substance; compensatory-to-division; rhetorician's means)
phase2_pass_log.pass_3_complete: Dedicated consubstantiation<->incorporation bridge subsection (definition; dual-axis map; divergences; player<->avatar/guild/faction identification grounding Attitude)

outline.title: Benign/malign range recap + Identification introduced
outline.summary: Carrying over from the Samson anecdote (RM-00), Burke notes rhetoric spans malign appeals (invective, polemic, eristic, logomachy — 'the Scramble') and benign ones (sacrificial love through to 'neutral' communication). He then proposes a dialectical raising of the level of generalization: an imagery of slaying is a special case of TRANSFORMATION, and transformation involves the ideas and imagery of IDENTIFICATION. Rhetoric is therefore to be 'reduced' to the wider-scope term identification, with killing/strife treated as a species of it (p.19-20). 'War' becomes a 'special case of peace' — not a primary motive but a derivative perversion of communion (p.20).

outline.title: Identification and "Consubstantiality"
outline.summary: The core substance-theoretic passage. A is not identical with his colleague B; but insofar as their interests are joined (or A is persuaded that they are), A is 'identified' with B (p.20). To identify A with B is to make them 'consubstantial' — 'substantially one' while each remains a distinct locus of motives, so each is 'both joined and separate, at once a distinct substance and consubstantial with another' (p.21). Burke links this explicitly to the Grammar (built on 'substance') and to the planned Symbolic (built on 'identity'); substance, though abolished by many modern thinkers as a term, retains its FUNCTION, because 'substance' in the old philosophies was an ACT, and a way of life is an 'acting-together' in which men share sensations, concepts, images, ideas, attitudes that make them consubstantial (p.21). Identification is then declared COMPENSATORY TO DIVISION: it is affirmed with earnestness precisely because there is division; if men were not apart there would be no need for the rhetorician to proclaim their unity (p.22). The titular term 'identification' thus carries, by the same token, its ironic counterpart: division (p.22-23). Rhetoric is 'concerned with the state of Babel after the Fall' (p.23).

outline.title: The Identifying Nature of Property
outline.summary: Metaphysically a thing is identified by its properties; rhetorically, identification is frequently by economic property. In surrounding himself with properties that 'name his number' or establish his identity, man is ethical — and 'Avarice' is the scenic word 'property' translated into an agent's ATTITUDE, or 'incipient act' (p.24). Moral growth is organized through properties (goods, services, status, citizenship, reputation, love), but property forming identity against other identity-forming entities breeds turmoil — hence Marxism and Veblen read as theorists of rhetoric (p.24). Persuasion = identifying your cause with another's interests; in 'pure identification' there would be no strife, and in absolute separateness none either — strife arises when identification and division are ambiguously joined (p.25), which is why, per Aristotle, rhetoric 'proves opposites' over the wavering line between 'cooperation' and 'exploitation' (p.25). Examples: the policy of the 'Scraped Plate'/food-as-policy and press 'screening' (Wallace) (pp.24-26); praising God or Science in terms that sanction one ownership-structure or imperialist-militarist expansion (Preen/Prone dialogue, 'John Q. Militarist-Imperialist') (pp.26-27).

outline.title: Identification and the "Autonomous"
outline.summary: Principle: an activity's reducibility to intrinsic autonomous principles does NOT free it from identification with extrinsic orders of motivation. The shepherd qua shepherd acts for the sheep, but may be 'identified' with raising them for market (p.27). 'Identification' names the autonomous activity's place in a wider context with which the agent may be unconcerned. Pure concentration on one integrated motive-structure = Symbolic; considering the identifications whereby a specialty makes one a participant in a social/economic class = Rhetoric ('Belonging' in this sense is rhetorical) (p.28). Stress on art's 'autonomy' can become a roundabout identification with a privileged class (Veblenian) or with political conservatism — 'whenever you find a doctrine of nonpolitical esthetics affirmed with fervor, look for its politics' (p.28). Historical shifts: Plato's thought (Winspear) and the Sophists were identified with different class-interests at different times (pp.28-29).

outline.title: The "Autonomy" of Science
outline.summary: Science as mere agency/instrument takes on the nature of the scenes, acts, agents and purposes with which it is identified; a faulty political structure can yield a 'perverted science' (concentration-camp specialists of National Socialist Germany) (p.29). The liberal apologist treats applied science as a good-and-absolute, circuitously endowing it with the philosophic function of God as the grounding of values; his thought vacillates between science-as-method and science-as-intrinsically-good-substance (p.30). An unavowed identification smuggles a theological function into a secular term, reinforcing occupational autonomy and the pragmatist notion that specialized work suffices as a grounding of morality (p.30-31). Conclusion: a science takes on the moral qualities of the movements with which it becomes identified; one's morality as a specialist cannot do duty for one's morality as a citizen (p.31).

outline.title: "Redemption" in Post-Christian Science + Dual Possibilities of Science
outline.summary: In a post-Christian, secularized era, the redemptive role (the Sacrificial King / Vessel laden with collective guilt) may be taken over by a SCAPEGOAT: anti-Semitism as the secularized replica of the Divine Scapegoat under Hitlerism, Jews 'magically identified' by many (p.31-32). A clinic/laboratory can become a 'secular temple' of concealed ritualistic devotion; the 'impersonal' scientific terminology slides from treating nature as 'things' to treating animals and then enemy peoples as 'things' — though they are persons (p.32). 'Dual Possibilities of Science' qualifies: Burke is NOT saying science must take on such malign identifications (Federation of American Scientists' attempt to dissociate atomic war-power from national security; the Gromyko/ownership paradoxes; the joke of the father who tells his son never to trust anyone). Good will is necessary but not sufficient; the morality of the specialty is 'no longer enough' under 'war potential' framing (pp.32-35).

outline.title: Ingenuous and Cunning Identifications
outline.summary: The rhetorical motive can operate WITHOUT conscious design by any agent: false or inadequate terms we impose on ourselves in varying deliberateness (self-protective and/or suicidal). Analogy to the psychologist's 'malingering' — a class not too exacting in scrutinizing flattering identifications practices a 'profitable malingering' (p.36). Rhetoric comprises both use (rhetorica utens, Demosthenes) and study (rhetorica docens, Aristotle's treatise) of persuasive resources (p.36). Protecting an interest by using terms 'not incisive enough to criticize it properly' brings rhetoric to the edge of CUNNING; Iago and Tartuffe are 'demons of Rhetoric'; Julien Sorel internalizes the rhetorical motive (hypocrisy-to-out-hypocritize-the-hypocrites) (pp.36-37).

outline.title: Rhetoric of "Address" (to the Individual Soul)
outline.summary: Even individual psychology has a strongly rhetorical ingredient: the Freudian dream evades the moralistic censor by stylistic subterfuge (analogue of literature under censorship); the ego/id confronting the super-ego is like an orator before a somewhat alien audience; the psyche is a 'parliament' (p.37-38). Rhetoric is thus ADDRESSED — and a man can be his own audience ('an I addressing its me', Mead) (p.38). Traditional rhetoric (Aristotle) stresses the external audience: lists of beliefs and character-traits with which the speaker favorably/unfavorably identifies cause and character (p.38). Socialization-as-moralizing is itself rhetorical: education exerts pressure from without, the individual completes it from within ('only those voices from without are effective which can speak in the language of a voice within') (p.39). Tanala tromba-seizure and the 'rhetoric of hysteria' (Kardiner) show even non-linguistic appeal is in origin addressed (p.39-40).

outline.title: Rhetoric and Primitive Magic
outline.summary: Witchcraft (Kluckhohn 'Navaho Witchcraft', Cassirer's Myth of the State) is brought within rhetoric's range. Against the scientist view (magic = early bad science), Burke insists rhetoric has 'no systematic location' in the bad-science/good-science antithesis: the basic function of rhetoric is 'the use of words by human agents to form attitudes or to induce actions in other human agents' — a 'call for help' is neither magic nor science but realistic and hortatory (p.41). Crucial formula: poetic language = symbolic action for itself; scientific language = preparation for action; RHETORICAL language = inducement to action — 'or to attitude, attitude being an incipient act' (p.42). The word-magic approach reverses the true order: magic was a FAULTY DERIVATION from a proper linguistic function — the realistic use of addressed language to induce action in PEOPLE was mistakenly transferred to induce motion in THINGS (pp.42-43).

outline.title: Realistic Function of Rhetoric
outline.summary: Anthropologists should recognize the rhetorical factor in their own field: magic-as-'primitive rhetoric' (a pragmatic device promoting social cohesion — Malinowski, Kluckhohn) is truer than modern-rhetoric-as-'survival of primitive magic'. Rhetoric is rooted not in any past social condition but in 'an essential function of language itself … the use of language as a symbolic means of inducing cooperation in beings that by nature respond to symbols' (p.43). It is a 'realism of the act' — moral, persuasive — not true/false in the propositional sense ('the rhetoric of witchcraft' discouraging rapid capital-accumulation among the Navaho) (pp.43-45). Closing recap (pp.45-48): rhetoric has two main aspects — its USE OF IDENTIFICATION and its NATURE AS ADDRESSED; identification implies division; persuasion re-enters ('Rhetoric is the art of persuasion'); 'there is no chance of our keeping apart the meanings of persuasion, identification (consubstantiality) and communication (the nature of rhetoric as addressed)' (p.46). Final note: identification between beings of unequal status can extend into the idealistic, out of which (later, on Order) arises 'a kind of magic or mystery' marking all human relations (p.48) — a forward seed to RM-03/RM-06.

concepts.label: identification (rhetoric's master term)
concepts.gloss: Rhetoric reduced from 'persuasion' to the wider-scope term 'identification': A is identified with B when their interests are (or are persuaded to be) joined; killing/strife is a species of it. Burke's titular redefinition.

concepts.label: consubstantiality / consubstantial
concepts.gloss: To identify A with B is to make them 'consubstantial' — 'substantially one' while each remains a distinct locus of motives; both joined and separate. The substance-theoretic ground of identification (p.21).

concepts.label: substance as act / acting-together
concepts.gloss: 'Substance' in the old philosophies was an ACT; a way of life is an 'acting-together' in which men share sensations, concepts, images, ideas, ATTITUDES that make them consubstantial (p.21). The function survives even where the term is abolished.

concepts.label: identification compensatory to division
concepts.gloss: Identification is affirmed with earnestness precisely because there is division; if men were not apart, no rhetorician would need to proclaim their unity (p.22). Division is identification's ironic counterpart.

concepts.label: division / Babel after the Fall
concepts.gloss: Men are individual loci 'at odds'; identification confronts the implications of division; rhetoric is 'concerned with the state of Babel after the Fall' (p.23). War = the 'ultimate disease of cooperation' (p.22).

concepts.label: Grammar–Rhetoric–Symbolic triad
concepts.gloss: Grammar built on 'substance' (universal paradoxes/placement); Rhetoric on identification ('substance' applied to persuasion/dissuasion, partisan classification); Symbolic to be built on 'identity' (unique individuals at peace) (pp.21-23).

concepts.label: transformation / reidentification
concepts.gloss: The 'filling' (killing) of a thing is the changing of it; stating its nature before and after the change is an identifying of it. Slaying = a special case of transformation, which involves identification's imagery (p.20).

concepts.label: identifying nature of property
concepts.gloss: Metaphysically a thing is identified by its properties; rhetorically, often by economic property. Surrounding himself with properties that 'name his number', man is ethical, but property-against-property breeds discord (pp.23-24).

concepts.label: Avarice as property-translated-into-attitude
concepts.gloss: 'Avarice is but the scenic word property translated into terms of an agent's ATTITUDE, or incipient act' (p.24). A scene→attitude/act translation — direct seed of the Attitude (6th) term in the Rhetoric.

concepts.label: rhetoric 'proves opposites'
concepts.gloss: Putting identification and division ambiguously together (where 'cooperation' ends and 'exploitation' begins cannot be scientifically fixed) is the characteristic invitation to rhetoric — why, per Aristotle, rhetoric 'proves opposites' (p.25).

concepts.label: identification by default (the autonomous)
concepts.gloss: An activity's reducibility to intrinsic autonomous principles does not free it from identification with extrinsic orders; to praise science without dissociating from its reactionary uses is to identify with them 'by default' (pp.27, 26-27).

concepts.label: 'Belonging' is rhetorical
concepts.gloss: Considering the identifications whereby a specialized activity makes one a participant in a social/economic class is to be 'in the region of rhetoric'; 'Belonging' in this sense is rhetorical (p.28). Class-identification through specialty.

concepts.label: look-for-its-politics (autonomy of art)
concepts.gloss: Affirmations of art's autonomy can become a roundabout identification with privileged-class or conservative interests: 'whenever you find a doctrine of nonpolitical esthetics affirmed with fervor, look for its politics' (p.28).

concepts.label: science as agency taking on identified motives
concepts.gloss: Science as mere agency/instrument takes on the nature of the scenes, acts, agents, purposes with which it is identified; a perverted political structure yields a perverted science (pp.29, 31). Agency-ratio reasoning.

concepts.label: unavowed (theological) identification
concepts.gloss: An identification can smuggle a theological function (God as grounding of values) into a term 'on its face wholly secular', as the liberal endows applied science with intrinsic goodness (p.30). Concealed substance-claim.

concepts.label: scapegoat / secularized Divine Scapegoat
concepts.gloss: In post-Christian science the redemptive/purgative role is delegated to a Vessel or scapegoat: anti-Semitism as the secularized replica of the Divine Scapegoat under Hitlerism; minorities 'magically identified' (pp.31-32).

concepts.label: rhetorica utens / rhetorica docens
concepts.gloss: Rhetoric comprises both the USE of persuasive resources (rhetorica utens, Demosthenes' philippics) and the STUDY of them (rhetorica docens, Aristotle's Art of Rhetoric) (p.36). Standard term-gloss.

concepts.label: ingenuous vs cunning identifications
concepts.gloss: The rhetorical motive can operate without conscious design (false terms we impose on ourselves — 'profitable malingering'); protecting an interest with terms not incisive enough to criticize it brings rhetoric 'to the edge of cunning' (pp.35-36).

concepts.label: rhetoric as addressed / self-address
concepts.gloss: Persuasion implies an audience, so rhetoric is ADDRESSED; a man can be his own audience ('an I addressing its me', Mead). Freud's psyche-as-parliament shows individual psychology's rhetorical ingredient (pp.37-38).

concepts.label: socialization as rhetorical (voice-within)
concepts.gloss: Socialization-as-moralizing is rhetorical: education presses from without, the individual completes it from within; 'only those voices from without are effective which can speak in the language of a voice within' (p.39).

concepts.label: attitude as incipient act
concepts.gloss: Rhetorical language is 'inducement to action (or to attitude, attitude being an incipient act)', distinguished from poetic symbolic-action and scientific preparation-for-action (p.42). The Rhetoric's clearest seed of the 6th dramatistic term.

concepts.label: magic as faulty derivation of rhetoric
concepts.gloss: Word-magic reverses the true order: the realistic use of addressed language to induce action in PEOPLE was mistakenly transferred to induce motion in THINGS; magic is a faulty derivation FROM rhetoric, not its ancestor (pp.42-43).

concepts.label: realistic function of rhetoric
concepts.gloss: Rhetoric is rooted in an essential function of language itself: 'the use of language as a symbolic means of inducing cooperation in beings that by nature respond to symbols' (p.43). A 'realism of the act', not propositional truth.

concepts.label: magic as primitive rhetoric / social cohesion
concepts.gloss: Magic's socializing aspect is better read as 'primitive rhetoric' — a pragmatic device assisting cultural survival by promoting social cohesion (Malinowski, Kluckhohn) — than modern rhetoric as survival of magic (p.43).

concepts.label: persuasion–identification–communication inseparable
concepts.gloss: Closing synthesis: 'there is no chance of our keeping apart the meanings of persuasion, identification (consubstantiality) and communication (the nature of rhetoric as addressed)' (p.46). The three are facets of one motive.

concepts.label: identification of unequal status → magic/mystery (seed)
concepts.gloss: Consubstantiality 'symbolically established between beings of unequal status' may extend into the idealistic, out of which (later, on Order) arises 'a kind of magic or mystery' marking all human relations (p.48). Forward seed to mystery/hierarchy.

positions.label: Rhetoric's master term is identification, not persuasion
positions.summary: Burke's titular move: by a dialectical raising of the level of generalization, rhetoric is 'reduced' to identification (wider scope), with persuasion/strife/killing as species. Persuasion re-enters at the end as one facet, not the genus.

positions.label: Identification is grounded in consubstantiality (shared substance/act)
positions.summary: To identify A with B is to make them consubstantial — substantially one yet distinct. Because substance was an act and a way of life is an acting-together, a doctrine of consubstantiality (explicit or implicit) 'may be necessary to any way of life'.

positions.label: Identification is compensatory to division
positions.summary: Identification is affirmed because men are divided; division is its ironic counterpart. Pure identification = no strife; absolute separateness = no strife; their ambiguous joining is the invitation to rhetoric.

positions.label: Identification operates unconsciously, by default, and through property/autonomy
positions.summary: Identification need not be designed: it works through property forming identity, through the 'autonomous' specialty's class-belonging, and through self-imposed inadequate terms ('by default', 'profitable malingering'). The rhetorical and the moral fuse where an undetected identification is revealed.

positions.label: Rhetoric is essentially addressed (incl. self-address) and realistic, not magical
positions.summary: Persuasion implies an audience; one can be one's own audience. Rhetoric's function — inducing cooperation in symbol-responsive beings — is realistic ('realism of the act'); magic is a faulty derivation of this function, mis-transferred to things.

positions.label: Rhetorical language is inducement to action OR ATTITUDE (attitude = incipient act)
positions.summary: The triad poetic(symbolic-action)/scientific(preparation)/rhetorical(inducement) explicitly names attitude as an incipient act — the operational seed of Burke's 6th dramatistic term and the hinge for grounding Calleja's Attitude/disposition layer.

pentad_term_tags.rationale: Substance was an ACT; a way of life is an 'acting-together'; consubstantiality is co-action. Identification is what makes a shared act possible.
Identification operates on the agent-locus: A identified with B; 'an individual locus of motives'; the human agent qua human agent participates in a larger unit of action beyond the specialty.
'Avarice' = the SCENIC word 'property' translated into agent-attitude; science takes on the nature of the scenes with which it is identified (scene-agency / scene-act ratios).
Science 'as mere instrument (agency)'; persuasion's stylistic identifications are the rhetorician's MEANS; rhetoric = the means of persuasion available in a situation.

Explicitly seeded: 'attitude being an incipient act' (p.42) and Avarice as property-as-attitude/incipient-act (p.24); acting-together shares 'attitudes' (p.21). This unit operationalizes the Rhetoric-side seed of the 6th term.

calleja_pim_candidates.rationale: Identification underlies player identification with avatar, character, guild, faction, and playerbase — Burke's 'acting-together' that makes agents consubstantial maps onto Calleja's micro-phase cohabitation/cooperation/competition and macro-phase guild/society sociality. Consubstantiality is the symbolic-substance mechanism beneath co-presence and group belonging ('Belonging is rhetorical', p.28).

Consubstantiation (substantially-one-yet-distinct via acting-together) is the rhetorical/symbolic homologue of Calleja's dual-axis incorporation (environment absorbed INTO consciousness; player absorbed INTO environment via avatar). The avatar is the single systemically-upheld locus through which player-and-gameworld become 'substantially one' while the player remains a distinct locus of motives — Burke's exact both-joined-and-separate structure.

Attitude-as-incipient-act (p.42) and acting-together's shared 'attitudes' (p.21) ground the affective/dispositional layer: identification recruits emotion (sacrificial love through to 'neutral' communication as desexualized love, p.19) as the binding tonality of consubstantial union.

Identifying one's cause with another's interests, and the 'proving opposites' over cooperation-vs-exploitation, maps to goal-alignment/competition dynamics; 'pure identification' = no strife is the limiting case of fully shared ludic goals.

interlocutors.function: rhetoric 'proves opposites' (p.25); rhetorica docens (p.36); the external-audience model of appeal and the point at which 'Aristotle begins his treatise' (p.46).
Marxism read as a study of capitalistic rhetoric / 'mystification'; property-and-ideology as rhetorical (p.24); forward to RM-03.
'theorist of rhetoric'; invidious class-identification via specialty/autonomy ('Veblenian lines', p.28); forward to RM-04.
dream-as-evasion-of-censor; ego/id/super-ego as orator/audience; Wit and Its Relation to the Unconscious — the 'third person' rapport — as 'the purest rhetorical pattern' (pp.37-38).
the self as 'an I addressing its me' grounds rhetoric-of-self-address (p.38).
witchcraft as ideology discouraging rapid capital-accumulation = 'rhetoric of witchcraft' promoting social cohesion (pp.40, 43-45).

interlocutors.author_year: A. Kardiner (The Individual and His Society)
interlocutors.function: Tanala tromba-seizure 'requires an audience' → 'rhetoric of hysteria' (pp.39-40).

interlocutors.author_year: Ernst Cassirer (The Myth of the State)
interlocutors.function: a book 'really about' the manipulation of belief for political ends in which 'rhetoric has no systematic location' — the scientist magic/science antithesis Burke rejects (pp.40-41).
magic as pragmatic device promoting social cohesion supports magic-as-primitive-rhetoric (p.43).
property as 'twy-streaming fount' / derived from Imagination — the dual moral aspect of property (p.24).

interlocutors.author_year: Stendhal (Le Rouge et le Noir / Julien Sorel); Molière (Tartuffe); Shakespeare (Iago, Macbeth)
interlocutors.function: 'demons of Rhetoric' and the internalized rhetorical motive / cunning identification (pp.36-37, 40).
the Grammar (substance) ↔ Rhetoric (identification) ↔ Symbolic (identity) architecture; consubstantiality carried over from the paradox of substance (pp.21-23).

tensions.label: Identification as union vs. identification as masking division
tensions.summary: Identification names a genuine sharing of substance (acting-together, consubstantiality) AND a strategic/cunning device that masks real division (eulogistic coverings, profitable malingering, identification 'by default'). Burke holds both: the same mechanism that binds a community can be 'cloaked malice'. The unit does not resolve whether consubstantiality is primarily ontological (men really are joined-and-separate) or rhetorical-strategic (men are persuaded they are joined). For the integration this is consequential: is player-avatar/guild consubstantiality a real phenomenological absorption (Calleja's incorporation) or a persuaded/symbolic belonging (terministic) — the bridge subsection treats this as the central divergence.

tensions.label: Substance abolished as term vs. retained as function
tensions.summary: Burke concedes 'substance' is an abstruse, paradox-ridden term that thinkers 'really did abolish … from their terminologies of motives', yet insists they cannot abolish its FUNCTION ('a doctrine of consubstantiality … may be necessary to any way of life'). The bridge to Calleja inherits this: Calleja never uses substance-vocabulary, yet incorporation performs the consubstantial FUNCTION (substantially-one-yet-distinct). The homology is functional, not lexical.

tensions.label: Rhetoric as realistic act vs. rhetoric extending into magic/mystery
tensions.summary: Burke insists rhetoric's function is 'wholly realistic' (inducing cooperation in symbol-responsive beings) and that magic is a faulty derivation from it — yet closes by granting that consubstantiality between beings of UNEQUAL status 'may extend far into the realm of the idealistic', out of which 'a kind of magic or mystery' arises (forward to Order/hierarchy). The realistic-function thesis and the mystery-seed sit in productive tension; the negative/hierarchy spine concepts enter here.

consubstantiation_incorporation_bridge.status_consolidated_from_grammar: Consolidates the bridge the Grammar pipeline flagged as 'pending-future-rhetoric-of-motives-pipeline' (gm-pentad-operationalization-manual Section E, incorporation_consubstantiation_bridge; gm-substance-vocabulary 'load-bearing seed'). RM-01 supplies the burke-direct textual ground the Grammar could only seed via GM-00 p.xix ('A may become non-A … consubstantial with non-A') and GM-02 type-16 'consubstantial-substance'.
consubstantiation_incorporation_bridge.a_what_consubstantiation_means_for_burke: To identify A with B is to make A 'consubstantial' with B (p.20): A is 'substantially one' with a person other than himself yet 'remains unique, an individual locus of motives' — 'both joined and separate, at once a distinct substance and consubstantial with another' (p.21). The ground is action: 'substance … was an act; and a way of life is an acting-together; and in acting together, men have common sensations, concepts, images, ideas, attitudes that make them consubstantial' (p.21). Consubstantiality is therefore (i) substance-theoretic (carried from the Grammar's paradox of substance), (ii) act-based (co-action, not static likeness), (iii) compensatory to division (affirmed because men are apart, p.22), and (iv) the very thing identification accomplishes — identification IS the making-consubstantial.

b_map_to_calleja_incorporation.claim: Burke's consubstantiation is the rhetorical/symbolic homologue of Calleja's dual-axis INCORPORATION (IG-10, canonical def. p.169): 'absorption of a virtual environment into consciousness, yielding a sense of habitation, supported by the systemically upheld embodiment of the player in a single location, as represented by the avatar.'
axis_alignment: Calleja AXIS 1 (environment absorbed INTO the player's consciousness) <-> Burke 'A is substantially one with' the other: the gameworld becomes part of the player's own structure of motives, as the other becomes 'substantially one' with A.

Calleja AXIS 2 (player absorbed INTO the environment via the avatar, a single systemically-upheld location) <-> Burke 'yet he remains unique, an individual locus of motives … both joined and separate': the avatar is precisely the locus through which the player is joined to the world while remaining a distinct substance.

Calleja SIMULTANEITY CONDITION (both axes concurrent or it reduces to mere involvement) <-> Burke's both-joined-AND-separate simultaneity: consubstantial union does NOT dissolve distinctness; the two substances are one in act yet two in being — the same paradox-of-substance simultaneity.
b_map_to_calleja_incorporation.shared_function: Both name the same dynamic — a being made 'substantially one' with something other than itself while remaining a distinct locus — reached from incommensurable traditions (Burke: substance-metaphysics + symbol-action; Calleja: experientialist embodied cognition, Lakoff+Johnson/Damasio). The homology is FUNCTIONAL, not lexical (Calleja never uses 'substance'; Burke never uses 'embodiment').

c_divergences: MEDIUM OF UNION: Burke = rhetorical/symbolic identification through shared SUBSTANCE — property, interests, ideology, terministic belonging ('Belonging is rhetorical', p.28). Calleja = phenomenological ABSORPTION through 6 involvement dimensions (kinesthetic, spatial, shared, narrative, affective, ludic) with the spatial+kinesthetic cornerstone.

ONTOLOGICAL STATUS: Burke's consubstantiality is ambivalently real-or-persuaded (T1: one can be 'persuaded to believe' interests are joined, p.20) and can be strategic/cunning ('by default', 'profitable malingering'). Calleja's incorporation is a sustained-but-fleeting EXPERIENTIAL STATE, not a persuaded belief — it either obtains phenomenologically or slips back to involvement.

GROUNDING THEORY: Burke grounds union in act/substance-metaphysics and a 'realism of the act'; Calleja grounds it in experientialist gestalts and consciousness-as-internally-generated-construct (Lakoff+Johnson 2003, Damasio 2000, Dennett 1991) — NOT in substance, NOT in Merleau-Ponty/Heidegger (those are ABSENT from IG-10).

DIRECTIONALITY EMPHASIS: Calleja insists on bidirectionality as a corrective to the unidirectional-plunge metaphor; Burke's consubstantiality is symmetrical-but-asymmetrically-deployed (the rhetorician engineers A's identification with B, often across UNEQUAL status, p.48) — closer to a persuasion-directed vector than to Calleja's mutual double-axis.

SCOPE: Burke's identification is society-wide and includes self-address (an I addressing its me, p.38) and unconscious/by-default operation; Calleja's incorporation is bounded to ergodic media that acknowledge the player's presence/agency (precludes non-ergodic media).

d_grounds_player_identification_and_atti.player_avatar_character: Identification (A consubstantial with B while remaining a distinct locus) is the symbolic mechanism beneath player-with-avatar/character identification: the avatar is the systemically-upheld locus through which the player is 'substantially one' with the gameworld yet remains a distinct locus of motives (Calleja embodiment-axis; PIM Shared involvement).
d_grounds_player_identification_and_atti.guild_faction_playerbase: Burke's 'acting-together' that makes men consubstantial, and 'Belonging is rhetorical' (p.28), ground player identification with guild/faction/playerbase — Calleja's Shared involvement (micro-phase cohabitation/cooperation/competition; macro-phase guild/society sociality, IG-06). Consubstantiality supplies the substance-theoretic WHY beneath Calleja's descriptive WHAT of co-presence and group belonging.
d_grounds_player_identification_and_atti.grounds_attitude: Attitude-as-incipient-act (p.42) and acting-together's shared 'attitudes' (p.21) make this unit the Rhetoric-side anchor of Burke's 6th dramatistic term: the player's disposition/stance toward avatar, guild, and gameworld is an incipient act of identification. This grounds the Affective/dispositional layer of the integration and the pentad's Attitude term simultaneously.
